texts: On day 0 of Year 1, Coraline Ash carried Pell's leather case on the Cliff Path.
Coraline Ash and Pell watched the sky-cat hunt at the East Row from the Middle Row.
Pell told Coraline Ash that surviving nightmoths flee to the dim lanterns of the Hollows.
Coraline Ash wrote Pell's explanation in the notebook.

q1_issues.issue: "Pell's explanation" is an event noun's underlying subject, which the instruction set routes to that noun's own subject role (Agent), not the opaque Possession.

q2_gaps: a passage-initial date frame ("On day 0 of Year 1, ...") whose temporal scope carries over the following sentences — only explicitly anaphoric temporal NPs ("that evening/night") are covered by term propagation, so the later sentences end up with no date at all
review.notes: The seal-projection table lists only Member/Name typing as projecting out of an attitude seal; statement 38 projects (GroupOf sk_lantern_1 lantern), the definite-plural analogue, which matches the denial-bundle rule but is not explicitly licensed there. Everything else in the sealed complement (the possessor link, both distribution rules) is placed correctly.

issues.reason: Complements of nouns and adjectives states that a genitive naming an event noun's underlying subject ("Marta's objection", "the committee's ruling") takes that noun's subject role, not Possession, and "Pell's explanation" is exactly that — Pell is the explainer — so (Possession sk_explanation_1 pell) asserts a relation the text never states.

gaps_confirmed: A passage-initial date frame ("On day 0 of Year 1, ...") whose temporal scope runs on over the following sentences has no carrier: term propagation is defined only for explicitly anaphoric temporal NPs ("that evening/night", "the following morning"), so the watching, telling and writing events end up with no date.
new_gaps: An epoch-style calendar reference ("day 0 of Year 1") has no Time term distinct from the Gregorian day-of-month: (Day 0) silently occupies the day-of-month slot with no Month to anchor it, and the seeded same-year-month day ordering would read it as a month-day.

The seal-projection interim table licenses only Member/Name typing to project out of an attitude seal; a DEFINITE PLURAL's typing atom is GroupOf (here (GroupOf sk_lantern_1 lantern) for "the dim lanterns"), which the table never names — a licensed form needs to say whether the group-typing analogue of Member projects.

A generic sealed under an attitude complement cannot carry its own truth value: the empirical 0.9/0.9 of "surviving nightmoths flee ..." is lost inside the Theme term, which stands at the wrapper's (STV 1.0 0.99). The prompt registers in-seal grammar as a limitation but names no form that preserves a sealed rule's strength.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form is (Agent sk_explanation_1 pell) in place of the emitted (Possession sk_explanation_1 pell) — the event noun's subject role, which the instruction set licenses directly; everything else in the parse stands.
adjudication.notes: The reviewer's "statement 46" indexes the typing atom; the offending atom is line 47 (expl_poss). The sealed complement is otherwise correctly built — fresh variables per sealed rule, the adjectival restriction as a premise conjunct, the possessor link kept inside, and only typing/Name/decomposition projected.
